title: SYZYGY RUNNER: a run-and-gun where dodging is automatic and stopping kills you (free, browser)
author: office-canard
selftext:
RUNNER is a free run-and-gun you can play in the browser.

SYZYGY



Play: [https://office-canard.itch.io/sigyzy](https://office-canard.itch.io/sigyzy)



You don't aim and you don't dodge. Your runner fires two pistols on his own and slips through the bullets by himself. You only do two things: keep moving, and time your jumps. Stand still and you're done.



The rest is machines. Pulleys hoist you up, belts and pendulums carry you, fans and catapults throw you into the sky, and you carry the speed from one device into the next. 100 stages, 19 kinds of devices.



Where it came from



It started with a YouTube video of a pulley. The first prototype was a puzzle. Then I wanted running, jumping and gunfights: the gun kata of Equilibrium, the shootouts in Johnnie To's films, the romance of running straight through a crowd of enemies firing at you. The hero began as a stick figure, and the world turned into cyberspace. For the music I picked the didgeridoo, said to be the oldest wind instrument in the world.



How AI fit in



\- Claude wrote the code: about 12,500 lines of JavaScript, its own physics for all 19 devices, and its own WebGL renderer. No physics or rendering library.

\- Everything you see is drawn in code. No image-generation AI, not even for the icon: it's an in-game shot with the muzzle flash added in code. The runner and enemy motion comes from Mixamo motion capture, converted to numbers by a tool Claude wrote.

\- All 21 sound effects are synthesized with Web Audio. The music is 6 tracks from Pixabay.

\- Stages: Claude built a tool that places one device, runs the stage from the start, measures where the runner lands, then places the next device or gap. I played them, cut one that was too easy, and ordered ST81-100 by how rarely I cleared each one.

\- Testing: a script runs all 100 stages start to finish on every commit. I played around 10,000 runs myself while debugging, and the game logs every run. When letting go of the windmill early at ST84 felt like it made me fall, Claude went through my log: 175 runs, and every fast landing had missed the zip line. We rebuilt the gaps.

\- Speed: the target was 60 fps on a slow Android phone. Before touching the game, Claude built a separate test page that searched how many enemies it could hold (4,372 on that phone). Only then did we move the whole game to WebGL.



Feedback welcome, especially on where you got stuck.
